sections.label: Part 1
sections.title: Beginner bookbinding courses
sections.subtitle: A phone call to an adult learning centre
sections.instructions: You will hear a woman called Ella ringing an adult learning centre to ask about bookbinding courses. Answer Questions 1-10 and complete the table. In the real test this recording is played once only; this practice part is set to play twice.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Part 1. You will hear a woman called Ella ringing an adult learning centre to ask about bookbinding courses. First, you have some time to look at questions one to five.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions one to five.

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: Good morning. Calderwood Learning Centre. Declan speaking.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: Oh, hello. I'm ringing about your bookbinding courses. I saw a poster in the library, but it didn't give many details.

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: Right. Well, I can help with that. Have you done any bookbinding before?

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: No. Nothing at all. I just like the idea of making my own books rather than buying them.

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: Then you've got three courses to choose from, and they're all for complete beginners. Shall I start with the Saturday taster?

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: Yes, please.

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: It's just one day, a Saturday, from morning till late afternoon. It's a good way to find out whether you enjoy it.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: Okay. And what do you actually make? A notebook, I suppose?

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: Not on the taster. No. The notebook's on the longer course. On the Saturday, you make a small album for photographs, that kind of thing. It's simple, but you finish it in a day.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: Oh, lovely. That would make a nice present.

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: A lot of people say that. And you don't need to be good at drawing or anything like that. It's mostly folding and sewing.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: Good. And how much is the taster?

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: It's forty-five pounds, and that includes all the materials, the paper, the card, the thread.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: Very reasonable.

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: It is. We try to keep the short courses cheap so that people give it a go.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: And who's the tutor?

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: That's Lydia Pinnock. She's been making books for years, and she's very patient with beginners.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: Sorry. Could you spell her surname?

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: Of course. P I n n o c k.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: Thanks. I like to know who I'll be learning from.

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: Fair enough. Now the next course is the evening course. That runs for six weeks on Tuesday evenings.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: Right.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: And that's where you make the notebook?

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: Yes. A proper notebook with a hard cover. You sew the pages together in the early weeks, then you learn to cover the boards with cloth.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: That sounds more like what I want, actually.

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: And in the final week, you make a box, so you've got somewhere to keep the notebook. People are always pleased with that.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: What a good idea. I've got a friend who'd love that. How much is the evening course?

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: A hundred and twenty pounds for the whole course. We do ask for a deposit when you book though, and then you pay the rest when the course starts.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: Fine. That's no problem at all.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions six to 10. Now listen and answer questions six to 10.

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: The last one is the summer school. That's five days, Monday to Friday, all day. So you get a lot done.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: In July, is it? I've got some time off then.

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: It was in July last year, but this year, it's August, near the start of the month.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: Ah, right. I see.

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: It's very relaxed. You work at your own pace, and there's a garden where people sit with their coffee when they need a break.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: Sounds nice. Is it a big group?

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: No. We keep it small. The maximum is eight people, so everyone gets plenty of help from the tutor.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: Good. I like that.

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: Yes. The tutor can spend time with everyone, so nobody's left waiting.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: That's what I'd want. And the cost for the week?

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: The summer school's a hundred and seventy-five pounds and that includes lunch every day in the cafe downstairs.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: Oh, that's handy. It saves people rushing out at midday.

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: Most of them just carry on chatting about their books.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: Do I need to bring anything with me?

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: Not tools. We provide all of those and you leave them here. But do bring an apron because there's a lot of glue and paint involved.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: I'll remember that. I've ruined enough clothes already. And how do I book?

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: Well, for most courses, you can book on the website. But for the summer school, you need to book by phone so we can check there's still a place.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: Right. Then I'd better decide quickly. Can I ring you back this afternoon?

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: Of course. Just ask for Declan.

segments.speaker: Ella
segments.text: I will. Thanks very much for your help.

segments.speaker: Declan
segments.text: Bye for now.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: That is the end of part one. You now have half a minute to check your answers.
